data.comment: Two blockers. (1) ADR-14: SHA-256 of an IP address is not anonymous - the IPv4 space can be enumerated, so this is still personal data and contradicts the product owner's answer to Q3. Use a keyed hash with a key that lives only in memory and rotates daily. (2) ADR-12: trusting X-Forwarded-For unconditionally lets any client pick its own identity and walk around the limiter. Trust it only when a proxy is explicitly configured, and then only the entry the proxy appended.

data.rationale: Use the socket address by default. Only when URLSHORTENER_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR is set, use the last entry of X-Forwarded-For - the address the trusted proxy itself observed. Consequences: Safe by default. Deployments behind a proxy must set one flag; deployments behind several chained proxies are not supported yet.

data.rationale: Identify a visitor as HMAC-SHA256(key, ip + user agent), where the key is random, held only in process memory and replaced every UTC day. Store the truncated digest; never store or log the key, the address or the user agent. Consequences: Identifiers cannot be reversed, linked across days or recomputed after a restart. Unique counts are per day only, and a restart or a second instance over-counts slightly; accepted in exchange for holding no personal data.
data.title: ADR-14: Unique visitors by a keyed hash under a daily-rotating in-memory key
